reasoning: Top-view SEM images at 0.5, 100 and 5 um scale bars, with inset domain-size histograms, show peaks near 0.1 um for PC, 10-100 um for HOC and 1e2-1e3 um for SC [obs1].
These histogram peaks establish that domain size spans four decades across the three growth states, from ~0.1 um (PC) through ~10-100 um (HOC) to ~1e2-1e3 um (SC) [n7].

Taking that domain-size ordering (PC smallest, HOC intermediate, SC largest) as given, the as-grown low-temperature photoluminescence data show PC exhibiting two emission branches plus an IR tail below 150 K across 50-370 uW at 80 K, HOC an intermediate response, and SC a single emission band [obs1].

This ranks the as-grown low-temperature emission complexity with the crystalline/domain state: PC shows dual peak plus IR tail, HOC is intermediate, and SC shows a single peak, tracking the same PC-HOC-SC ordering used for domain size [n13].

The chain as a whole reads the microstructural size series (step 1) and the optical emission series (step 2) as ordered together by growth state, with PL splitting most pronounced in the smallest-domain material and absent in the largest-domain (single-crystal) material [writer inference].
end_to_end.why_weakest: obs1 is reused to support both n7 (size) and n13 (optical ranking), so the step assumes the size ordering from step 1 lines up with the PL ordering rather than the source directly stating a size-to-emission link.
